mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on (a) Team A's possession FOR being above its own historical mean and (b) Team B's corner_kicks AGAINST being above competition context mean. Both conditions must hold simultaneously — neither alone is sufficient.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A corner_kicks FOR rises when both conditions are jointly satisfied, and the joint effect exceeds the sum of each single-condition effect.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production is jointly conditioned on both its own possession dominance and the opponent's (Team B's) corner-kick concession rate: when Team A holds high possession AND faces a side that concedes many corners, Team A's corner output rises beyond what either dimension alone predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) from two different teams evaluated simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band, nor to a simple venue or opponent-descriptor split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compare Team A's corner_kicks FOR in FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF, conditioned on Team A's possession FOR being above competition context mean. The half-level split is the structurally novel element — not just a full-match average.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's second-half corner share (corners in 2H relative to 1H) rises with possession dominance, more so than the competition-context baseline half-split would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production shows a within-match half-level asymmetry: its second-half corner share relative to first-half corners is associated with its possession level, such that teams with high overall possession generate a disproportionately larger share of corners in the second half.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) split jointly conditioned on a continuous possession dimension — not a single observable with one coarse band. It requires both half-resolution data and a second observable (possession) as the conditioning variable.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute Team A's shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR ratio (shot accuracy) and Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST / shots AGAINST ratio (concession accuracy). Condition jointly: when Team A's accuracy is above its own historical mean AND Team B's concession accuracy is above competition context mean, test whether total shots_on_target in the match is elevated.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total match shots_on_target rises when Team A's shot accuracy and Team B's shots-on-target concession rate are jointly elevated, beyond what either team's marginal average predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetry between Team A's shots-to-shots-on-target conversion rate (shot accuracy) and Team B's shots-on-target concession rate jointly predicts whether the match's total shots-on-target volume deviates from the competition baseline — specifically, when one side has high shot accuracy and the other concedes many shots on target, total shots-on-target is elevated beyond what either team's single-observable average implies.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a ratio of two observables (shots_on_target / shots) as the conditioning variable, applied asymmetrically across the two teams — not a single observable with one band. The joint cross-team ratio structure is not covered by any single-observable mirror or simple split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on (a) Team B's fouls FOR being above competition context mean and (b) Team B's goals AGAINST being above its own historical mean (proxy for trailing/chasing context). Both conditions must hold simultaneously. Measure cards_2h FOR in the second half.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's cards_2h FOR rises when both high foul rate and elevated goals-against context are jointly present, more than either condition alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half card accumulation (cards_2h) is jointly associated with both its foul rate and the goal differential context: when Team B commits fouls at an above-average rate AND is in a match where goals scored against it are elevated (i.e., it is chasing the game), its second-half card rate rises beyond what either foul rate or goal context alone predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine three-observable joint relationship (cards_2h, fouls, goals) with a within-match period split (second half). It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band — it requires two distinct conditioning observables simultaneously.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute each team's yellow_cards FOR / fouls FOR ratio (card-per-foul rate). When the two teams' card-per-foul ratios diverge substantially (one team is much more card-prone per foul than the other), test whether total cards_2h in the match is elevated relative to competition context.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total match cards_2h rises as the cross-team divergence in yellow_cards-per-foul ratio increases, reflecting that one team's structural card-proneness amplifies second-half card accumulation beyond what raw foul counts alone predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The cross-team asymmetry in yellow card accumulation versus foul rate — specifically, Team A's yellow cards FOR relative to its fouls FOR compared to Team B's yellow cards FOR relative to its fouls FOR — identifies whether one side is systematically more card-prone per foul committed, and whether this asymmetry is associated with elevated total second-half cards in the match.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a ratio of two observables (yellow_cards / fouls) computed for each team and then compared asymmetrically across teams — a cross-team, two-observable ratio structure. It is not reducible to a single observable mirror or a simple opponent-descriptor band.
